non_issues.claim: The Sites tests disable the first-line origin check by patching the name in hud_api, which only works because daemon imports check_origin inside the function; if that import moved to module level the tests would quietly cover the wrong check and still pass.
non_issues.why_not: The claim says hoisting the import would leave the shift undetected, but the suite would catch it. All five Sites tests patch the same name, `jarvis.v2.hud_api.check_origin`. If the import moved to module level, the patch would stop working and `check_origin` would run first in `_dispatch`. For a forged Host it answers 403 'untrusted Host' (hud_api.py:1410-1411). `test_a_hud_only_approval_is_answered_only_from_a_real_host` expects 404 with 'owner HUD' for each forged Host. That response can only come after the first line has been bypassed, so this test would fail. That failure shows the patch no longer works for the whole class. The claim that all five tests would still pass silently is wrong, and nothing in the current code is defective.
non_issues.source: pooled cluster p1, ruled invalid, accepted as a non-issue by lead on 2026-10-23

non_issues.claim: All seven listener Host checks now go through one shared helper in a config file that the write gate does not protect, so one edit there turns off every DNS-rebinding guard together.
non_issues.why_not: The owner-approved cleanup plan (CL-3) asks for exactly this: one shared helper, `config.own_host_header`, that replaces the seven inline Host-header copies. The guard's logic is unchanged (an exact match on two spellings), and the helper is pinned by a unit table plus a mutation test that makes the per-listener refusal tests fail if it is loosened. The seven listener files that held the copies were not on the SELF_PROTECTED write-protected list either, so the change adds no unprotected route that did not already exist. Putting all the call sites behind one helper is the intended design, not a defect.
